subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: For manually configured public Remote Domain endpoints, should iOS authenticate the gateway through normal CA-plus-hostname validation instead of binding the endpoint to one TLS leaf fingerprint?
rationale: The current behavior blocks valid anycast certificate rotation, but changing or removing the pin alters the identity boundary protecting a client that may execute gateway-directed actions; repository history does not establish the intended permanent policy.

options.title: Use public-PKI identity
options.body: Use CA and hostname validation for manually entered public DNS endpoints while retaining pinning for self-signed, private, or discovery-derived endpoints, with a stored-pin migration.

options.title: Keep explicit pinning
options.body: Retain strict leaf identity and document Cloudflare anycast endpoints as unsupported unless a stable origin certificate is exposed.

options.title: Introduce a selectable trust mode
options.body: Add an explicit in-app endpoint trust choice, accepting the extra configuration and upgrade surface needed to distinguish PKI validation from pinning.

recommendation.title: Use public-PKI identity
recommendation.body: Use CA and hostname validation for manually entered public DNS endpoints while retaining pinning for self-signed, private, or discovery-derived endpoints, with a stored-pin migration.

likelyOwner.reason: The most focused current-main ownership signal is the existing iOS certificate-rotation recovery implementation.
